name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Jim Baird running for reelection
Huge financial imbalance: Baird raised $358k with $537k outside support vs. Cox's $20k
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Baird's incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage make a Democratic upset implausible; markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. Drew Cox's minimal fundraising gives no evidence of a competitive campaign.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or unexpected outside spending surge against Baird could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent Jim Baird is seeking another term after easily securing renomination. The partisan lean of about fifteen points Republican, combined with the usual incumbency advantage, makes this one of the safer Republican holds on the House map this cycle.

The financial picture underscores the imbalance: Baird has raised roughly $358,000 and benefits from over half a million dollars in outside support, while Democrat Drew Cox has raised only about $20,000 with no outside backing. Prediction markets give Baird roughly a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The main question is the size of Baird's victory margin, not the outcome.
